title: Survival Italian for Visitors
shortDescription: The Italian you need for a trip: airport, transport, hotel, restaurants, shopping, sightseeing and emergencies — with speaking practice.
description:
A short, practical course for tourists, business travellers and family visitors. In 8 short units you practise the real situations of a trip to Italy: passport control, train tickets and taxis, checking in at a hotel, ordering food (including vegetarian and halal-friendly requests), shopping, asking the way, the pharmacy and emergencies, and making Italian friends.

Every unit has picture words with audio, a speaking role-play where you answer out loud, and a quick review with a printable study sheet.
objectives:
Get through the airport and passport control
Buy tickets and use taxis, trains and buses
Check in at a hotel and solve problems in your room
Order food and explain what you do not eat
Shop, ask prices and sizes, and pay
Ask for directions and handle a health emergency

lessons.title: Passport control
lessons.summary: Answer the officer's questions politely.

blocks.title: The situation
blocks.body: You have just landed in Rome. The officer at passport control asks you a few questions. Answer in Italian — tap a suggestion or say it out loud.

lines.speaker: Officer
lines.english: Good morning. Passport, please.

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Good morning. Here is the passport.

lines.speaker: Officer
lines.italian: Qual è il motivo del viaggio?
lines.english: What is the reason for your trip?

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: I'm here for tourism.

lines.speaker: Officer
lines.english: How long are you staying in Italy?

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: I'm staying two weeks.

lines.speaker: Officer
lines.english: Where are you staying?

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: In a hotel in Rome.

lines.speaker: Officer
lines.english: All right. Enjoy your stay!

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Thank you, goodbye!

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: Officials always use the formal **Lei**: *Dove alloggia?* (Where are you staying?). Answer with short, clear sentences — that is perfectly polite.

exercises.prompt: They say: “Buongiorno. Passaporto, per favore.” — what do you answer?
exercises.explanation: Buongiorno. Passaporto, per favore. (Good morning. Passport, please.) → Buongiorno. Ecco il passaporto. (Good morning. Here is the passport.)

exercises.prompt: They say: “Qual è il motivo del viaggio?” — what do you answer?
exercises.explanation: Qual è il motivo del viaggio? (What is the reason for your trip?) → Sono qui per turismo. (I'm here for tourism.)

exercises.prompt: They say: “Va bene. Buona permanenza!” — what do you answer?
exercises.explanation: Va bene. Buona permanenza! (All right. Enjoy your stay!) → Grazie, arrivederci! (Thank you, goodbye!)

exercises.prompt: They say: “Dove alloggia?” — what do you answer?
exercises.explanation: Dove alloggia? (Where are you staying?) → In un albergo a Roma. (In a hotel in Rome.)

lessons.title: Ordering a meal
lessons.summary: Book a table, order and ask for the bill.

blocks.title: The situation
blocks.body: You walk into a trattoria in Bologna with a friend. The waiter comes to you.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.english: Good evening! How many of you are there?

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: There are two of us.

lines.english: Please, have a seat. Here is the menu. Something to drink?

lines.english: Are you ready to order?

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Perfect, I'll have the tagliatelle.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.english: Is everything OK? Would you like a dessert?

lines.speaker: You
lines.italian: No, grazie. Il conto, per favore.
lines.english: No, thank you. The bill, please.

lines.speaker: Waiter
lines.english: Right away. Are you paying together or separately?

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Together, by card.

items.italian: Un tavolo per due, per favore.

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: In restaurants you will often see **coperto** on the bill: a small cover charge per person for bread and service. It is normal. Tipping is not required.

lessons.title: Asking the way
lessons.summary: Find the Colosseum with the help of a local.

blocks.title: The situation
blocks.body: You are lost near Piazza Venezia in Rome and want to go to the Colosseum. You stop a lady on the street.

lines.speaker: Local
lines.english: Yes? Do you need help?

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Excuse me, where is the Colosseum?

replies.english: Excuse me, how do I get to the Colosseum?

lines.speaker: Local
lines.italian: È vicino! Vada sempre dritto per Via dei Fori Imperiali.
lines.english: It's near! Go straight on along Via dei Fori Imperiali.

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Is it far on foot?

lines.speaker: Local
lines.italian: No, dieci minuti a piedi. Lo vede alla fine della strada.
lines.english: No, ten minutes on foot. You see it at the end of the road.

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Perfect. And for the tickets?

lines.speaker: Local
lines.italian: La biglietteria è a sinistra dell'ingresso.
lines.english: The ticket office is on the left of the entrance.

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Thank you very much, very kind!

lines.speaker: Local
lines.english: You're welcome, enjoy your visit!

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: If people speak fast, it is fine to say **Più piano, per favore** (more slowly, please). Italians are usually happy to help visitors who try their language.

exercises.prompt: They say: “No, dieci minuti a piedi. Lo vede alla fine della strada.” — what do you answer?
exercises.explanation: No, dieci minuti a piedi. Lo vede alla fine della strada. (No, ten minutes on foot. You see it at the end of the road.) → Perfetto. E per i biglietti? (Perfect. And for the tickets?)

exercises.prompt: They say: “La biglietteria è a sinistra dell'ingresso.” — what do you answer?
exercises.explanation: La biglietteria è a sinistra dell'ingresso. (The ticket office is on the left of the entrance.) → Grazie mille, molto gentile! (Thank you very much, very kind!)

exercises.prompt: They say: “Sì? Ha bisogno di aiuto?” — what do you answer?
exercises.explanation: Sì? Ha bisogno di aiuto? (Yes? Do you need help?) → Scusi, dov'è il Colosseo? (Excuse me, where is the Colosseum?)

exercises.prompt: They say: “È vicino! Vada sempre dritto per Via dei Fori Imperiali.” — what do you answer?
exercises.explanation: È vicino! Vada sempre dritto per Via dei Fori Imperiali. (It's near! Go straight on along Via dei Fori Imperiali.) → È lontano a piedi? (Is it far on foot?)

lessons.title: At the pharmacy
lessons.summary: Explain your symptoms and buy medicine.

blocks.title: The situation
blocks.body: You have had a headache and a slight fever since this morning. You go into a pharmacy.

lines.speaker: Pharmacist
lines.english: Good morning, how can I help?

lines.speaker: You
lines.italian: Buongiorno. Ho mal di testa e un po' di febbre.
lines.english: Good morning. I have a headache and a slight fever.

lines.speaker: Pharmacist
lines.english: Since when?

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Since this morning.

lines.speaker: Pharmacist
lines.english: Are you allergic to any medicine?

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: No, no allergies.

lines.speaker: Pharmacist
lines.italian: Prenda questo: una compressa ogni otto ore, dopo i pasti.
lines.english: Take this: one tablet every eight hours, after meals.

lines.speaker: You
lines.italian: Una compressa ogni otto ore. Grazie.
lines.english: One tablet every eight hours. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Pharmacist
lines.italian: Se la febbre non passa, vada dal medico.
lines.english: If the fever doesn't go away, see a doctor.

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: All right. How much is it?

items.english: My … hurts / I have a … ache

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: Emergency numbers: **112** for everything (police, ambulance, fire). If your passport is lost or stolen, report it at the police (**denuncia**) and contact your embassy.

lessons.title: Meeting an Italian
lessons.summary: Chat with a friendly Italian at a café.

blocks.title: The situation
blocks.body: You are sitting at a café in Naples. The young man at the next table starts a conversation.

lines.speaker: Luca
lines.english: Hi! Are you here on holiday?

lines.speaker: You
lines.italian: Sì, sono in vacanza per una settimana.
lines.english: Yes, I'm on holiday for a week.

replies.italian: No, lavoro qui da un mese.
replies.english: No, I've been working here for a month.

lines.speaker: Luca
lines.english: Nice! Where are you from?

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: I'm Indian, from Mumbai.

lines.speaker: Luca
lines.english: Do you like Naples?

lines.speaker: You
lines.italian: Sì, mi piace molto! La pizza è buonissima.
lines.english: Yes, I like it a lot! The pizza is excellent.

replies.italian: Sì, è bellissima, ma fa caldo!
replies.english: Yes, it's beautiful, but it's hot!

lines.speaker: Luca
lines.italian: Ah, la pizza di Napoli è la migliore! Io mi chiamo Luca.
lines.english: Ah, Neapolitan pizza is the best! My name is Luca.

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Nice to meet you, Luca! I'm Arjun.

replies.english: Nice to meet you! My name is Sana.

lines.speaker: Luca
lines.italian: Stasera c'è un concerto in piazza. Vuoi venire?
lines.english: Tonight there's a concert in the square. Do you want to come?

lines.speaker: You
lines.english: Gladly! What time?

lines.speaker: Luca
lines.italian: Alle nove. Mi dai il tuo numero?
lines.english: At nine. Will you give me your number?

replies.english: Yes, I'll text you on WhatsApp.

items.english: Will you give me your number?

blocks.title: Good to know
blocks.body: Italians love talking about **food** and **football**. A compliment about the local food is the best way to start a conversation!

exercises.prompt: They say: “Alle nove. Mi dai il tuo numero?” — what do you answer?

options.text: Sì, mi piace molto! La pizza è buonissima.

exercises.explanation: Alle nove. Mi dai il tuo numero? (At nine. Will you give me your number?) → Certo, è 333 123 4567. (Sure, it's 333 123 4567.)

exercises.prompt: They say: “Ti piace Napoli?” — what do you answer?

options.text: Sì, mi piace molto! La pizza è buonissima.

exercises.explanation: Ti piace Napoli? (Do you like Naples?) → Sì, mi piace molto! La pizza è buonissima. (Yes, I like it a lot! The pizza is excellent.)

exercises.prompt: They say: “Stasera c'è un concerto in piazza. Vuoi venire?” — what do you answer?

options.text: Sì, sono in vacanza per una settimana.

exercises.explanation: Stasera c'è un concerto in piazza. Vuoi venire? (Tonight there's a concert in the square. Do you want to come?) → Volentieri! A che ora? (Gladly! What time?)

exercises.prompt: They say: “Ciao! Sei qui in vacanza?” — what do you answer?

options.text: Sì, sono in vacanza per una settimana.

exercises.explanation: Ciao! Sei qui in vacanza? (Hi! Are you here on holiday?) → Sì, sono in vacanza per una settimana. (Yes, I'm on holiday for a week.)
